opener: Lord, nobody around me knows how long I've actually been carrying this — they see the version of me that still shows up, still smiles in the doorway, still says "I'm managing" when they ask, and they have no idea it's been years, not days, since this last felt light.
paragraphs: I've tried the things people recommended. I've waited out the timeline doctors and friends and my own patience all promised would work. And still, underneath the managing, the same ache keeps returning like it never actually left the room. I'm tired of treating a twelve-year problem like it should respond to a twelve-minute prayer, and I'm tired of pretending I'm fine with the in-between.

So tonight I'm done waiting for the crowd around me to clear before I come to You. I don't need an audience's permission to reach — I just need to press through whatever's standing between us, even if all I can touch is the edge of what You're wearing. You didn't ask the woman in the Gospel for her file, her diagnosis, or her twelve years of explanations before You healed her — You only asked for her faith to reach. So here is mine, reaching past everyone and everything in the way: if I may but touch You tonight, I will be made whole. Let whatever has been quietly draining me dry up for good, the same way it dried up for her — straightway, completely, with nothing left to relapse into. In Jesus' name, amen.
